 Updated: 12:00 PM EDT Oct 23, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Danielle Scruggs South Florida voters can track early voting, mail ballot deadlines and polling sites county by county ahead of Election Day, Nov. 3. 
 The Get the Facts Data Team is tracking early and mail-in ballots. The data comes from the University of Florida Election Lab .

 Palm Beach County
 Early voting is Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
 Early voting locations are as follows:
 Belle Glade — Belle Glade Library/Civic Center — 725 NW Fourth St.
 Boca Raton — Boca Raton Downtown Library — 400 NW Second Ave.
 Boca Raton — Glades Road Branch Library — 20701 95th Avenue S.
 Boca Raton — Spanish River Library — 1501 Spanish River Blvd.
 Boca Raton — Sugar Sand Park Community Center — 300 S. Military Trail
 Boca Raton — West Boca Raton Branch Library — 18685 state Road 7
 Boynton Beach — Canyon Branch Library — 8915 Sen. Joe Abruzzo Ave.

 Jupiter — Jupiter Community Center — 200 Military Trail
 Lake Worth — Lantana Road Branch Library — 4020 Lantana Road
 Lake Worth — Palm Beach State College Main Campus — 4200 S. Congress Ave.

 On Election Day, you must vote at your assigned polling place. To find yours, click here . 
 The deadline to request a mail-in ballot was Thursday, Oct. 22, at 5 p.m.
 Secure vote-by-mail ballot boxes will also be available at the main office on Election Day. All ballots must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day to count.
 Ballots can be tracked by clicking here .
 For more information, click here .

 Martin County
 Early voting is from Wednesday, Oct. 21, until Saturday, Oct. 31, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. at all six early voting locations. 
 Elections Center — 135 SE Martin Luther King, Jr. Blvd., Stuart
 Elisabeth Lahti Library — 15200 E. Thelma Waters Ave., Indiantown
 Hobe Sound Library — 10595 SE Federal Highway, Hobe Sound
 Hoke Library — 1150 Jack Williams Way, Jensen Beach
 Peter & Julie Cummings Library — 2551 SW Matheson Ave., Palm City
 Robert Morgade Library — 5851 SE Community Drive, Stuart 
 The deadline to request a mail-in ballot was Oct. 22 at 5 p.m.
 Stay up to date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 
 St. Lucie County
 Early voting is Monday, Oct. 19, through Saturday, Oct. 31, from 10 a.m. until 6 p.m. daily, including Sunday, Oct. 25. 
 Early voting locations are as follows: 
 Fort Pierce — Renaissance Business Park (Formerly Orange Blossom Business Center) — 4132 Okeechobee Road
 Fort Pierce — Zora Neale Hurston Library — 3008 Avenue D
 Port St. Lucie — Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence — 500 NW California Blvd.
 Port St. Lucie — MIDFLORIDA Credit Union Event Center — 9221 SE Event Center Place
 Port St. Lucie — Paula A. Lewis Library — 2950 SW Rosser Blvd.
 Port St. Lucie — Port St. Lucie Community Center — 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.
 Port St. Lucie — Robert E. Minsky Gym: New Location — 750 SW Darwin Blvd. 
 Fort Pierce — Lakewood Park Branch Library — 7605 Santa Barbara Drive
 The deadline to request a mail-in ballot was Oct. 22 at 5 p.m.
 Port St. Lucie mayoral candidates discuss growth and investment in debate Around the country: National coverage from WPBF 25 News 
 Indian River County
 Early voting is Monday, Oct. 19, through Saturday, Oct. 31, from 8 a.m. until 4 p.m. Extended hours are Thursdays from 8 a.m. until 6 p.m. 
 Early voting locations are as follows:
 Sebastian — Sebastian City Hall Council Chambers — 1225 Main St.
 Vero Beach — Indian River County Main Library — 1600 21st St.
 Vero Beach — Indian River County Supervisor of Elections Office — 4375 43rd Ave.
 Vero Beach — Intergeneration Recreation Center (Room 112) — 1590 Ninth St. SW
 The deadline to request a mail-in ballot was Oct. 22 at 5 p.m. 
 Follow us on social: Facebook | X | Instagram | YouTube | TikTok 
 Okeechobee County 
 Early voting is Saturday, Oct. 24, through Saturday, Oct. 31, from 8:30 a.m. until 6 p.m.
 Early voting locations are as follows:
 Okeechobee — Historic Courthouse — 307 NW Fifth Ave. 
 The deadline to request a mail-in ballot was Oct. 22 at 5 p.m.
 The deadline to register to vote was Monday, Oct. 5.
